column1: This table classifies all World Bank member countries (189) and all other economies with populations of more than 30,000.

For FY27 (July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027), income groups are defined using 2025 GNI per capita (Atlas method): low income (LIC) ($1,175 or less); lower middle income (LMC) ($1,176–$4,635); upper middle income (UMC) ($4,636–$14,375); and high income (HIC) (above $14,375). Income classifications set on July 1 remain in effect until the next July 1.

IDA countries are those that lack the financial ability to borrow from IBRD. IDA credits are deeply concessional—interest-free loans and grants for programs aimed at boosting economic growth and improving living conditions. IBRD loans are noncessional. Blend countries are eligible for IDA credits because of their low per capita incomes but are also eligible for IBRD because they are financially creditworthy.

The Fragile and Conflict-Affected Situations (FCS) classifications from 2005 onward are derived from the FCS Lists available at https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/fragilityconflictviolence/brief/harmonized-list-of-fragile-situations. The FY27 classification will be incorporated following its official release.
The term country, used interchangeably with economy, does not imply political independence but refers to any territory for which authorities report separate social or economic statistics.
